title: Races, deadlocks, and memory visibility
hook: A race happens when two threads read and write shared state without coordination. A deadlock happens when threads wait on each other forever. Memory visibility is whether one thread sees another thread's writes — the .NET memory model guarantees visibility after proper synchronization.

blocks.text: A data race: thread A and B both increment _count without synchronization — you lose updates. A deadlock: thread A holds lock1 waiting for lock2 while thread B holds lock2 waiting for lock1. Visibility: without lock or volatile, CPU caches may let one thread see stale values — though lock and Interlocked establish proper ordering in practice.

entries.plainDefinition: Outcome depends on unpredictable thread scheduling when shared state lacks synchronization.
entries.example: Two threads incrementing a counter without lock lose one increment.

entries.plainDefinition: Circular wait where each thread holds a resource another needs.
entries.example: A waits on B's lock while B waits on A's lock.

entries.plainDefinition: Rules for which writes one thread observes from another.
entries.example: Exiting a lock ensures subsequent reads see prior writes inside the lock.

blocks.text: RabbitMQ consumers on multiple threads sharing a non-thread-safe Dictionary corrupt internal buckets. Deadlocks under load freeze services — often from lock ordering bugs or locking then awaiting messaging I/O. ConfigureAwait(false) in libraries avoids deadlocks with UI SynchronizationContext; ASP.NET Core has no context but lock-order bugs remain.

blocks.title: Deadlock prevention
blocks.body: Acquire locks in a fixed global order. Never await while holding a lock. Use timeouts on WaitAsync when appropriate.

snippet.label: Lost update race
snippet.explanation: Read-modify-write without synchronization loses updates under parallel handlers.

snippet.label: Lock ordering deadlock
snippet.explanation: Consistent lock ordering prevents circular wait. Prefer one lock or concurrent collections instead.

snippet.label: Unsafe shared dictionary
snippet.explanation: Dictionary is not thread-safe for concurrent writes. Use ConcurrentDictionary or message passing.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Assuming Dictionary is safe because reads are common. Different lock order in two methods. Using .Result after locking — blocks pool threads and worsens deadlocks.

interviewTakeaways: Races need shared mutable state without proper synchronization.
Deadlocks need circular lock waits — fix with ordering or fewer locks.
Prefer concurrent collections and Channels over hand-rolled locked dictionaries.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS avoids many races on the main thread but worker_threads and Atomics introduce the same concerns as C#.
